name: Graph Enrichment Shock: Sentinel Added at Day 45

asset_criticality.note: Pre-enrichment: CMDB but no Entra integration

threat_intel_enrichment.note: Pre-enrichment: Splunk TI only, no Sentinel Defender data

device_trust.note: Pre-enrichment: no Defender endpoint data, high device noise

environment_shifts.description: GRAPH ENRICHMENT EVENT (not an attack): Customer connects Microsoft Sentinel at Day 45. Entity resolution links 340 new identities (Entra ID → Splunk mapping). Factor noise drops: threat_intel_enrichment from 0.15 to 0.08 (Defender TI feeds added), device_trust from 0.20 to 0.12 (Defender for Endpoint data). Category distribution shifts: cloud_infrastructure increases from 14% to 22% (Sentinel generates cloud-native alerts Splunk didn't see). Total alerts_per_day increases from 180 to 250. The graph goes from 2800 entities to 5200 in one day.

business_context: THE REALISTIC DAY 45 SCENARIO for every v6.0 customer. Customer starts with Splunk. First 45 days: centroids calibrate on Splunk-only data. At Day 45, Sentinel connects. Three simultaneous changes: (1) 340 entity resolution links created, entity_resolution_completeness jumps 0.62→0.88, (2) factor noise drops for threat_intel and device_trust because Defender data is cleaner, (3) category distribution shifts because Sentinel alerts have different mix. QUESTION: Do centroids BENEFIT (lower noise → faster convergence per Bridge B) or TEMPORARILY DEGRADE (calibrated to old noise profile, factor distributions shifted)? This tests the transition dynamics that every multi-SIEM customer will experience.

name: Graph Enrichment Shock: Defender for Endpoint at Day 30

asset_criticality.note: Pre-enrichment: medical devices untagged, no endpoint agent

device_trust.note: Pre-enrichment: NO endpoint agent, medical devices unknown trust

environment_shifts.description: GRAPH ENRICHMENT EVENT (not an attack): Customer enables Defender for Endpoint at Day 30. All managed endpoints get agent. Device trust noise drops from 0.28 to 0.10 (now have real-time device health). Asset criticality noise drops from 0.22 to 0.13 (endpoint agent reports installed software, patch level). No change to category distribution — same alert sources. 1200 new device entities resolve against existing Sentinel identities.

business_context: CLEANER enrichment scenario than 2G-GE1. Only factor noise changes (device_trust and asset_criticality drop dramatically), NOT category distribution. This isolates the noise reduction effect from the category shift effect. If centroids benefit immediately (no accuracy dip), the transition is smooth. If there's a dip, it's because centroids calibrated to NOISY device_trust factors now see CLEAN values at different absolute positions. Bridge B Phase B predicts faster convergence at lower noise — but the TRANSITION may temporarily confuse calibrated centroids.
